acme_dev: Hey team, running into a CORS + auth problem when calling Redwood Node TS SDK from a Vercel Edge function. keep getting 403 on the POST and a preflight failure in the browser console.

maya: sorry to hear that — can you paste the exact error you see in devtools and the Edge function logs? also which SDK version are you using?

acme_dev: Error in browser console: "Access to fetch at 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate' from origin 'https://app.acme.com' has been blocked by CORS policy: Request header field authorization is not allowed by Access-Control-Allow-Headers."
Edge func logs (vercel): 
POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate 403 { message: 'invalid api key' }
Using @redwood/inference-js v0.9.1 imported in our edge function bundle.

oliver: quick note — we don't support direct browser usage of the server SDK (v0.x) because it sends the API key from client bundles. Did you intentionally import from the edge/browser build?

acme_dev: We're importing with: 
```ts
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
export default async function handler(req) {
  const res = await client.generate({ prompt: 'hi' });
  return new Response(JSON.stringify(res));
}
```
We set runtime: 'edge' in vercel.json.

maya: couple things to flag: 1) If the edge function runs on Vercel Edge, it executes at the edge and your code runs in a browser-like runtime. The NodeJS SDK may use Node-specific http libs causing different bundling behavior. 2) The browser CORS error indicates the browser is making the request directly to api.redwood.example (is that from the client or via your edge function?).

acme_dev: The browser calls our edge route at https://app.acme.com/api/gen which proxies to Redwood. The preflight shows the browser OPTIONS goes to api.redwood.example (not our route) — I think Vercel edge is trying to call Redwood directly from the user's browser? Not sure.

samir: that sounds like a bundling issue — the client bundle may have the Redwood request URL inlined and the browser is calling the upstream API instead of your edge route. Check your build output for any direct api.redwood.example calls. Also confirm your edge function returns proper CORS headers.

acme_dev: Good call. In our deployed bundle the call site has "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" referenced in the JS. We definitely didn't expect that. How would the SDK end up inlining the upstream URL?

oliver: likely because the SDK is resolving api base at build time and the bundler (esbuild/webpack) in the edge build included the full URL in the client bundle. The v0 SDK's HTTP client picks baseURL from options and might be serialized. The edge/browser variant of the SDK exports a tiny wrapper that uses global fetch and doesn't embed secrets or base URL the same way.

maya: repro steps please so we can escalate if it's a bug: 1) small repo (or gist) with minimal import 2) vercel.json + edge function 3) package.json showing sdk version and bundler. If you can't share, can you run this local repro?

acme_dev: I'll create a minimal repo, but here's a quick repro we ran locally with vercel dev: 

Edge function code:
```ts
// api/gen.ts (edge)
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: DENO_ENV_REDWOOD_KEY });
export default async (req: Request) => {
  const r = await client.generate({ prompt: 'test' });
  return new Response(JSON.stringify(r), { headers: { 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin': '*' } });
}
```
Browser call:
```js
fetch('/api/gen', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ prompt: 'x' }) })
```
Result: browser preflight  OPTIONS -> api.redwood.example (not /api/gen), and the API returns 403 with invalid api key.

oliver: thanks — this is consistent with the SDK exposing the upstream URL at runtime in the bundle. Short-term fixes: 1) don't import the server SDK in code that ships to the browser; 2) move the call into a Vercel Serverless (node) function (not edge) that runs on Node and can safely use the server SDK; or 3) use the SDK's browser/edge build if available (import path like `@redwood/inference/edge` or `@redwood/inference/browser`), which relies on global fetch and doesn't inline sensitive data.

samir: adding to that — SDK v1.2.3+ includes an explicit `edge` entrypoint that we recommend for Vercel Edge and CF Workers. Can you try switching to `import { createEdgeClient } from '@redwood/inference/edge'` and using that? It will use global fetch and not embed the full upstream URL in client bundles.

acme_dev: I tried `@redwood/inference/edge` and the bundle size dropped and the request now goes from our Edge function to Redwood (server-side) — no browser preflight. But now vercel logs show: `TypeError: globalThis.crypto is undefined` when running on Vercel Edge.

maya: that's a compatibility thing — Cloudflare/Edge runtimes expose web crypto differently. Vercel Edge should have globalThis.crypto, but if running in a local dev environment or older edge runtime it might be missing. We can work around by polyfilling or using a fallback in our edge wrapper.

oliver: can you paste the stack trace? Also mention runtime version in vercel.json. If it's prod only, include the deploy id.

acme_dev: stack: 
```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'getRandomValues')
 at node_modules/@redwood/inference/edge/dist/index.js:45:12
```
runtime in vercel.json: "edge". Deployment id: dpl_8a7f9

samir: ok this is something we saw — the edge build expects globalThis.crypto.getRandomValues for idempotency keys. CF Workers use `crypto.getRandomValues` but local vercel dev might not. For prod if Vercel Edge is missing it might be a runtime mismatch. Workarounds: 1) add a tiny polyfill at the top of your edge handler: `globalThis.crypto = globalThis.crypto || { getRandomValues: (arr) => { /* use Math.random fallback */ }}` (not ideal for security but fine for non-production dev). 2) ensure you're on Vercel's new Edge runtime that exposes web crypto. 3) use a node serverless function instead of edge.

acme_dev: thanks. One more thing: we saw intermittent 429s and our code retries aggressively which caused billing concerns on our side. Any best practices for retries from Edge?

maya: yes — for edge/workers keep retries conservative. Use exponential backoff with jitter and cap at 2 retries for non-idempotent text-generation. If you need higher reliability, route to Dedicated/Private capacity or implement server-side batching. Also set rate-limit headers to detect quota errors. We can also check your account logs for spikes and suggest limits.

acme_dev: ETA for SDK fix to avoid baseURL inlining and to improve crypto detection?

oliver: we have a patch queued — v1.2.4 will: (a) provide clearer entrypoints (`/edge`, `/browser`, `/node`), (b) avoid inlining baseURL into bundles, and (c) include an optional internal crypto fallback that throws a helpful error if missing. I'll escalate to eng-runtime and tag the PR.

edge-bot: ticket #SUP-2891 created and assigned to eng-runtime (oliver). Please attach minimal repro.

maya: for now recommended action for acme_dev: 1) switch to `@redwood/inference/edge` entrypoint, 2) verify runtime exposes crypto (or polyfill in dev), 3) ensure API key is never bundled client-side (use edge/server proxies), 4) add retry cap and backoff. Let us know the repro link and we'll prioritize the SDK patch. :thumbsup:

acme_dev: Thanks everyone — I'll send the minimal repo and attach it to SUP-2891. Appreciate the quick triage!
